text:
alex: quick check-in — picking up from the heap-lineage RFC. i want to confirm the pool boundary semantics we discussed yesterday

morgan: short recap pls? missed the meeting.

alex: idea is we tag each allocation with a compact "origin token" (4B) that records the logical heap lineage: caller pool id + allocation intent (scratch/persistent/cache)

alex: runtime can then use that token to group co-located blocks during compaction and to prefer migrating whole lineages to the same residency tier

sasha: sounds useful for defrag but worried about metadata bloat + lookups on the hot path. adding 4B per alloc multiplies for small boxes.

priya: can we make token optional? e.g. only for allocations above X or for arenas that enabled lineage?

alex: yes, plan A was per-arena opt-in. small fastpath allocs keep current header; big arenas enable lineage and pay overhead

morgan: tradeoff: if too many arenas opt out, lineage loses usefulness for global compactness. fallback: have a secondary sampling mode where we retroactively tag via allocation-chained samples?

alex: good point. we sketched a hybrid: default arenas sample 1/1024 allocations and write a sidecar map keyed by pointer region -> origin token. that keeps per-alloc overhead low but gives us enough signal for the defrag planner.

sasha: sidecar map needs evict strategy. also must survive migrations and be fast to query at free time. hashmap + coarse region keys?

alex: coarse-region (e.g., 64KB buckets) lookup at free time should be constant-ish. worst-case we miss lineage for tiny allocations but that's acceptable.

priya: what about offload + residency? if lineage groups go to host staging, we want to avoid scattering their fragments across multiple host pools. so lineage should be an affinity hint for the admission controller and the evictor.

morgan: admission controller change is straightforward: when receiving an evict decision, consult token -> preferred host pool. but policy must avoid hard pinning; keep soft affinity and allow spill for capacity pressure.

alex: exactly — token is a hint not a hard contract. we need a grace window so a lineage can be rehomed gradually instead of atomically moving all fragments and triggering spikes.

infra-bot: deploy-check: runtime/allocator lineage branch passes unit + perf smoke on dev cluster (heaplineage/branch/ci#42)

alex: perf numbers on sampling mode look good: median alloc latency +0.5% and p99 +2% in worst-case. memory overhead measured ~0.6% on our benchmark mix.

sasha: still need to define API for rollout: arena flag, sampling rate, bucket size, eviction affinity weight. propose defaults: sample 1/2048 for small arenas, 64KB bucket, affinity weight 0.3

priya: agree on defaults, but we need an operator knob for affinity weight per-tenant. enterprise customers will want stronger guarantees.

morgan: and a compatibility plan for existing on-disk snapshot formats — lineage sidecar must be exportable or reconstructible on restart. maybe checkpoint lineage mapping every N seconds and store in compact form.

alex: checkpointing plan: we persist only hot region tokens and rebuild rest lazily. on restart, unlabeled regions default to no-affinity until warmed.

sasha: question for long-term: could lineage tokens help model-aware placement (e.g., keep kv-cache allocations with the same model shard)? potential followup RFC.

alex: yes, put that in TODOs. immediate next steps: 1) land opt-in arena flag + sampling sidecar, 2) add admission affinity hook, 3) telemetry for lineage hit/miss and compaction benefits.

priya: i'll own telemetry. i'll add counters: sampled_allocs, sidecar_hits_on_free, lineage_compacted_bytes, affinity_moves

morgan: i'll prototype admission hook and affinity weight config.

sasha: i'll run compaction sims with synthetic fragmentation patterns to pick good defaults.

alex: sweet. if no objections i'll mark RFC follow-up and schedule a quick sync next Tue. :thumbsup:

morgan: +1

priya: +1

sasha: +1

alex: filing notes -> https://go/internal/heaplineage/followup (TODO: flesh out checkpoint format)
